recovery_profile: Standard — recover within 4 hours; up to 1 hour of data loss
performance_target: Typical API responses under 2 seconds — planning goal to validate
private_client_access: A new secure remote-access path is needed
authentication_requirement: Employees plus external Volunteers — fictional dev accounts
non_relational_store: Cosmos DB — preferred primary document store
notification_channels: Mobile push capability — fictional/dev testing only
Dev simulation only — no outbound delivery

notification_delivery_scope: Simulation-only MVP — defer email/push transports, retain functional channel intent
messaging_events: None — no separate messaging/event service required
supporting_services: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + Log Analytics — preferred diagnostics products
Azure Container Registry — preferred container image registry
sku_app_service: No SKU preference — Architect choose least-cost suitable tier meeting captured requirements
sku_nosql: No SKU preference — Architect choose least-cost suitable tier meeting captured requirements

current_notification_scope_resolution: The original notification_channels and brief notification_intent remain historical answers. The actual subsequent notification_delivery_scope explicitly resolves them: application simulation only in dev MVP; no email/push transport provisioning or outbound delivery; email/push functional intent deferred, not discarded. Simulation implementation is application-team scope.
current_delivery_scope: New dev-only hosting-platform MVP; first usable infrastructure within two weeks. Future Production is outside this delivery.
current_delivery_data_constraint: Development uses fictional data only. Mandatory security/privacy baseline applies in dev; future Production GDPR requirement remains outside this dev delivery, with no compliance certification.
system_description: Infrastructure-only hosting platform and cloud services for a secure, intuitive, mobile-first Volunteer engagement MVP, including support for a containerized backend. All application development is handled by another team and is out of scope.
business_objective: Reduce manual coordination and administrative overhead; improve Volunteer engagement and matching, opportunity discovery, assignments, approvals, tracking, reporting, visibility and communication; accelerate assignments and grow without proportional administration.
delivery_context: New MVP; pro bono initiative for The Organization. Existing coordination relies on calls, email, instant messaging, spreadsheets and manual approvals/follow-ups, causing overhead, low visibility and poor scalability. This is business context, not a migration request.
infrastructure_scope: Hosting support for a containerized backend; backend code excluded
Notification platform capabilities, with channels still to evaluate
Store anonymous resulting documentation in this repository
application_scope_exclusions: Detailed business workflow, escalation and reporting implementation
application_role_constraints: Initial permission boundaries require Project Stakeholders validation. Manager is a functional role, not an identifiable party. Exact permissions and application implementation belong to another team.
configurable_workflow_intent: Volunteer registration, participation approval, assignment confirmation, cancellations and changes. Exact rules and escalation remain undefined, belong to the application team, and do not block platform intake.
operational_reporting_intent: Opportunities, registrations, assignment status, completed activities and participation. Detailed reports and impact metrics require application stakeholder confirmation.
technology_evaluation_constraints: Candidates are not mandatory selections. Evaluate alternatives for suitability, security, simplicity, maintainability, scale and cost within limited nonprofit budgets; challenge complexity and avoid overengineering.
design_preferences_not_decisions: Prefer managed services and a modular monolith; no microservices absent clear justification.
data_processing_constraints: Personal Volunteer information and sensitive organizational activity may be processed. Beneficiary data is not assumed. Never use real personal information in development or testing; fictional sample data only.
security_privacy_requirements: Secure authentication and role-based access control
Encryption in transit and at rest
compliance: GDPR required for Production. MVP must be GDPR-aligned; the supplied brief says MVP does not have to be compliant. This release distinction does not waive applicable legal duties or mandatory security/privacy controls. Do not certify compliance.
anonymity_requirements: Anonymous generated source, documentation, commits, issues, pull requests, test data, infrastructure-as-code and artifacts
No customer/nonprofit or technology-partner names, individual names, real domains, organizational identifiers, correspondence or real beneficiary/Volunteer information
Use only generic party labels: The Organization, Technology Contributors, Volunteers, Coordinators, Administrators, Project Stakeholders
Do not request real names, personal emails, domains or identities during discovery
Do not publish repository remote URLs or account identities in project documentation
Author attribution uses agent role only; no people
recommendation_provenance_requirement: Reasonable recommendations must be labelled Assumption/Recommendation, never represented as user-confirmed values or permission.
initial_sku_pin_evidence: No SKU locks were volunteered in the original brief; this was not an explicit no-preference response.
sku_pin_evidence: Completed applicable Phase 3j: LRS is the sole exact pin; explicit no-SKU-preference answers for App Service and Cosmos; on-demand only; dev only with no override. Supporting-product preferences add no creative-SKU class under the service-menu mapping.
authorized_current_activity: Bounded Step 1 requirements discovery, anonymous documentation, validation and the required independent review through the interactive parent. No Azure reads or writes, credential operations, deployment, infrastructure code, application scaffolding, commits or pushes are authorized.
